findings.claim: Inside the section headed 'Jessica's Elopement (Act 2, Scenes 3-6)': "Shakespeare presents this as a romantic escape ('I shall be saved by my husband; he hath made me a Christian')".
findings.truth: That line is Act 3, Scene 5, spoken to Launcelot long after the elopement. Reworded to name Act 3.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg line 2756 'I shall be saved by my husband. He hath made me a Christian.' falls inside SCENE V of ACT III (lines 2727-2868).

findings.claim: Shylock, taunted by Solanio and Salerio about Jessica's elopement...
findings.truth: In Act 3 Scene 1 the two taunters are Solanio and Salarino. Salerio is a separate character who appears later. The lesson's own flashcard already says 'Salarino and Solanio', so the body text contradicts it.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg ACT III SCENE I opens 'Enter Solanio and Salarino.' (line 1909); speech prefixes SOLANIO / SALARINO throughout.

findings.claim: In the section headed 'Antonio's Ships Are Lost (Act 3, Scene 1)': "Shylock's response is chilling: 'I will have my bond.' He repeats this phrase obsessively".
findings.truth: The phrase Shylock repeats three times in Act 3 Scene 1 is 'let him look to his bond'. 'I'll have my bond' is the phrase he repeats obsessively in Act 3 Scene 3. Quotation swapped for the Act 3 Scene 1 line.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 1980-1982 (3.1): 'let him look to his bond' x3; lines 2551-2568 (3.3): 'I'll have my bond' x4.

findings.claim: For the OCR J352 extract question...
findings.truth: Banned spec code.

findings.claim: Shylock comes to court... The Duke appeals to his mercy, but Shylock refuses: 'I'll have my bond; I will not hear thee speak.'
findings.truth: That line is Act 3, Scene 3 - Shylock says it to Antonio in the street, with the gaoler present, before the trial. It is not a reply to the Duke and it is not in the trial scene. A student citing it as trial-scene evidence would lose the reference. Replaced with Shylock's actual first answer to the Duke, 'I have possessed your Grace of what I purpose' (4.1).
findings.evidence: Gutenberg line 2563 'I'll have my bond. I will not hear thee speak.' sits in ACT III SCENE III (2538-2602), addressed to Antonio. Line 2929 'I have possess'd your Grace of what I purpose' is Shylock's reply to the Duke in ACT IV SCENE I.

findings.claim: The Duke addresses Shylock as 'an inhuman wretch,' revealing prejudice even in the language of the court.
findings.truth: The Duke says it to Antonio in his opening speech, before Shylock has been called into court ('Go one and call the Jew into the court' comes after). He describes Shylock; he does not address him. The point about court prejudice still holds and is kept.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 2882-2887 (4.1): DUKE to ANTONIO, 'thou art come to answer / A stony adversary, an inhuman wretch'.

findings.claim: After the trial, Antonio is silent.
findings.truth: Antonio is not silent after the trial. He speaks in Act 4 Scene 1 to press Bassanio to hand over the ring, and he speaks again in Act 5. What is true is that he never celebrates and gets no triumphant speech; the sentence was rewritten to say that.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg lines 3615-3618 (4.1, after Portia and Nerissa exeunt): ANTONIO 'My Lord Bassanio, let him have the ring. / Let his deservings and my love withal / Be valued 'gainst your wife's commandment.'

findings.claim: Practice question 6: 'Explain the significance of Antonio's silence after the trial.'
findings.truth: Built on the same false premise as F15. Reworded to 'Antonio's lack of any triumph after the trial', which the mark scheme already describes ('has no triumphant speech').

findings.claim: Section heading 'The Ring Plot (Act 4, Scene 2 - Act 5)'.
findings.truth: The ring plot starts in Act 4 Scene 1: Portia asks Bassanio for the ring straight after the trial, he refuses, Antonio persuades him and Gratiano is sent after her. Scene 2 is only Nerissa collecting Gratiano's ring. Heading corrected to Act 4, Scene 1.
findings.evidence: Gutenberg ACT IV SCENE I runs 2871-3632 and contains Portia's request and Antonio's persuasion (3615-3622); SCENE II is 3633-3679.

findings.claim: Lorenzo speaks of the 'music of the spheres' - the idea that the universe is governed by divine harmony.
findings.truth: The phrase 'music of the spheres' does not appear anywhere in the play. Lorenzo's actual lines are 'There's not the smallest orb which thou behold'st / But in his motion like an angel sings' and 'Such harmony is in immortal souls'. The quotation marks made a critical term look like a quotable line; they have been removed.

findings.claim: 'Let his deservings and my love withal / Be valued against your wife's commandment.'
findings.truth: The text reads "Be valued 'gainst your wife's commandment". Restored.

findings.claim: Jessica is present in Belmont but largely silent in Act 5.
findings.truth: Jessica has roughly half of the 'In such a night' duet that opens Act 5 and says 'I am never merry when I hear sweet music'. She falls silent only once the other characters arrive. 'Largely silent' is loose rather than wrong across the whole act, and the lesson says two paragraphs earlier that she and Lorenzo exchange those lines. Not edited; a rewrite would ripple into the key fact, the exam tip, a practice question and a flashcard.

summary: No lesson was clean. Two substantive quotation errors: Shylock's 'I'll have my bond; I will not hear thee speak' presented as a trial-scene reply to the Duke when it is Act 3 Scene 3 to Antonio (L4, HIGH), and 'music of the spheres' quoted as Lorenzo's words when the phrase is not in the play (L5). Also Salerio for Salarino in Act 3 Scene 1, the Duke's 'inhuman wretch' given the wrong addressee, a false claim that Antonio is silent after the trial, Nerissa called a lawyer rather than a clerk, the ducat called a gold-silver alloy, and the ring plot dated to Act 4 Scene 2. Exam layer: 18 literal 'OCR J352' strings plus one 'Component 02', banned 'Level N' band names in three tips, 24 '4 marks' labels sitting on 8-mark ladders, 12 malformed ladders in L7-L8, and a 45-minute plan for a question worth about an hour. All AO claims check out against the spec, including that AO4 is assessed on this question.
